instructions: The day before, or at least 4 hours ahead: heat the oven to 350°F. Grease an 8-inch springform or round cake pan with the butter.
Spoon the ricotta into a sieve set over a bowl and let it drain for 15 minutes.
In a large bowl, whisk the drained ricotta with 1/4 cup plus 1 tbsp of the honey, the eggs, the cornstarch and the vanilla until smooth with no lumps.
Pour the batter into the pan and smooth the top.
Bake for 30 to 35 minutes, until the top is browned and the middle no longer wobbles.
Let the pie cool in the pan for 5 minutes. Take it out of the pan and let it cool completely. Cover it and refrigerate for at least 2 hours.
In the morning, cut the pie into 8 slices. Drizzle with the remaining 3 tbsp honey and dust with the cinnamon. Serve cold or after 15 minutes at room temperature.
Cover the leftover slices and refrigerate. They keep for up to 3 days. For longer, freeze the slices without honey for up to 1 month and thaw them in the fridge overnight.
advance_prep_notes: Bake the pie the day before and chill it
method_notes: Souvlaki For The Soul (the lead) makes a crustless pie of ricotta, honey, eggs and a little cornstarch, baked until set and drizzled with more honey and cinnamon; it is scaled here to one 15 oz tub for an 8-inch pan. Kopiaste and Easy World Recipes agree it is crustless and baked around 350°F (180°C), and Easy World Recipes says to drain ricotta first, which is why that step is here. The fridge and freezer times come from Easy World Recipes. The smaller pie bakes a little faster than the full size one.
